description: Nordic nutrient flow analysis (N, P, K) — imports, losses, and recovery potential per country
methodology: Material Flow Analysis (MFA) based on NIBIO, SSB, Norsk Vann, Frontiers P-MFA studies (Hamilton et al. 2023), HSY Finland, Svenskt Vatten, DTU Environment. Cross-validated with P27 (avlopsanlegg) and P29 (gjodselimport) from Perplexity Runde 2, 20.04.26. Order-of-magnitude estimates, not official statistics.

realized_recovery.headline: Realisert gjenvinning er minimal vs. potensialet

items.label: Realisert i dag (f.eks. VEAS Asker)
items.value: ~0,75 kt N / 0,28 kt P gjenvunnet fra avløpsslam

items.label: Teknisk potensial (alle strømmer)
items.value: 64 kt N / 9,8 kt P (25–30 % av import)

aquaculture_to_fjord.note: Frontiers P-MFA (Hamilton 2023): 80-90% of feed-P ends as discharge; N-loss ~35-45 kt/yr as dissolved ammonium/urea and particulate organic N

svartvann_to_sea.note: Population-based: 4.5 kg N, 0.6 kg P, 1.0 kg K per person/yr (Jenssen & Skjelhaugen 1994, confirmed by recent Nordic estimates). SSB reports net P-discharge after treatment at 1.48 kt/yr and N at 19.5 kt/yr

husdyr_to_environment.note: NIBIO/Miljodirektoratet: total husdyrgjodsel ~80-90 kt N/yr, 20-40% lost as NH3 to air and nitrate runoff. P-loss 10-20% of husdyrgjodsel-P via erosion and drainage

matavfall_to_incineration.note: NORSUS matsvinn ~417 kt/yr (2020); assuming 2-3% N and 0.3-0.5% P in mixed food waste sent to incineration

recovery_potential.note: 70% technical recovery factor applied to total loss streams (ambitious but feasible on 20-30yr horizon). Svartvann alone can replace 10-15% of mineral-N and 20-30% of mineral-P

reference_facilities.name: VEAS Asker
reference_facilities.technology: Chemical P-removal, biogas, slam to agriculture/landscaping. >90% P-removal from influent

reference_facilities.name: Helsingborg RecoLab (H+ Three Pipes)
reference_facilities.technology: Separate collection of svartvann/gravann/matavfall; anaerobic digestion, ammonia stripping, struvite precipitation. P-recovery >80-90%, N-recovery 50-70% demonstrated

SLU/RISE MFA studies on Swedish agriculture

imports.note: Denmark has strict N/P-balance requirements in agriculture (Baltic Sea Action Plan). High utilization of husdyrgjodsel.

aquaculture_to_fjord.note: Danish aquaculture relatively small; strict regulation

husdyr_to_environment.note: Denmark has highest husdyr-N utilization in Norden due to strict regulation, but still significant losses

matavfall_to_incineration.note: Denmark has extensive biogas infrastructure (175 plants, 8100 GWh/yr) reducing incineration losses

recovery_potential.note: Danish practice: 70-90% of P in wastewater ends in slam spread on agricultural land. N-recovery 20-40% via biogjodsel/slam. Multiple fullskala struvite plants operational

reference_facilities.name: HSY Viikinmaki
reference_facilities.technology: Biological N and P removal, sludge digestion, drying, composting. Composted slam used as soil product. ~4-5% of P and 34-40% of N remains in treated effluent

Helda/Helsinki University: Finnish wastewater nutrient study

nordic_summary.key_insight: 30-50% of imported N/P/K could theoretically be replaced by recovered nutrients from aquaculture, wastewater, and food waste streams. Norway alone loses ~91.5 kt N and ~14 kt P/yr across all streams, of which ~64 kt N and ~10 kt P are technically recoverable with maturing technology.

technologies.name: Ammonia stripping
technologies.note: Used in Helsingborg RecoLab and multiple Nordic pilot plants. Produces ammoniumsulfat for direct use as N-fertilizer. Requires high pH and concentrated streams

technologies.name: Struvite precipitation (MgNH4PO4)
technologies.note: Multiple fullskala plants in Denmark (Aaby, Herning). Produces slow-release fertilizer from reject water with high P-concentrations. Also captures some N and Mg

technologies.name: Source-separating toilets (urinsortering)
technologies.note: Demonstrated at Helsingborg H+ / RecoLab. Vacuum toilets + separate piping. Challenge is building/network infrastructure, not technology per se. Swedish LCA shows potential to cover 75% of national N-need

technologies.name: Biological N and P removal (activated sludge)
technologies.note: Standard in Nordic wastewater treatment. Removes 70-90% P and 50-80% N from influent. P ends in slam; N largely lost as N2 via denitrification unless combined with stripping

technologies.name: Chemical P-precipitation (Fe/Al)
technologies.note: Very mature and widespread in Nordic countries. P ends in slam with limited plant-availability. VEAS uses this approach with >90% P-removal

technologies.name: Thermal hydrolysis / pasteurization
technologies.note: Enabling technology for safe land-application of slam/biogjodsel. Does not affect N/P quantity but is prerequisite for agricultural use

technologies.name: IMTA (Integrated Multi-Trophic Aquaculture)
technologies.note: Blue mussels, kelp (tare) capture dissolved N/P from salmon cage effluent. Technical recovery 30-60% of P and 20-40% of N from aquaculture discharges assessed as feasible by 2030-2040

technologies.name: Biogas + digestate (anaerob utraatning)
technologies.note: Mature in Denmark (175 plants). Converts food waste and manure to biogas + digestate-fertilizer. Majority of N/P/K retained in digestate if spread on land. Logistical rather than technical barriers limit scale

technologies.name: P-recovery from mono-incinerated sludge ash
technologies.note: Under evaluation in EU sludge directive revision. Higher short-term agronomic P-efficiency than direct slam application. Requires dedicated mono-incineration infrastructure
